title: EOS POC capacity proposal and runbook
content:
Purpose:
This note is a concise deployment proposal and runbook for the EOS customer POC. Focus: dedicated GPU capacity sizing, practical autoscaling rules for the POC, and a short set of GPU cost sensitivity estimates. Goal is to get a realistic baseline for latency SLOs and monthly unit cost for their chat/assistant workload.

Executive summary:
- Recommended baseline: 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool for the 2-week POC burst, with aggressive autoscale headroom up to 10 GPUs for load spikes.
- Autoscaling policy: scale on effective tokens/sec demand and request queue length; use a combination of concurrency and token-rate triggers to avoid costly overprovisioning.
- Fallbacks: quantized model variant (8-bit) and a lower-RTT smaller model for graceful degradation.
- Expected incremental monthly cost (if steady-state at baseline): ~USD 16k–20k depending on cloud pricing and preemption. POC duration estimates provided below.

Customer context and workload profile (assumptions from discovery):
- Use case: customer-facing chat assistant integrated into web and mobile apps, mixed chat and short completions for task automation.
- Peak daily traffic window: 09:00–11:30 and 18:00–21:00 local; peak fraction ~30% of daily requests.
- Request mix: 70% short completions (avg 40 tokens output, 60 tokens input), 30% multi-turn chat (avg 80 tokens output, 120 tokens input).
- Target p50 latency: <120ms token latency for streaming; p99 tail target: <400ms for end-to-end response for 95% of requests.
- Traffic target for POC: steady 120 rps with bursts to 400 rps for up to 10 minutes.

Key sizing inputs and working assumptions:
- Average tokens per request (round-trip): short 100 tokens, chat 200 tokens. Weighted avg ~130 tokens/request.
- Server-side batching: effective average batch size assumed 4 for low-latency config, can be raised to 12 in throughput-optimized mode.
- Token throughput per GPU (approx): A10G ~ 3.5k tokens/sec single-stream steady (low latency config); A100-40GB ~ 9k tokens/sec; H100 (latest perf) ~ 12k tokens/sec. These are conservative estimates that account for mixed sequence lengths and KV cache overhead.
- Safety margin: plan to operate at <=60% sustained GPU capacity to keep headroom for variance and tail latency.

Baseline capacity calculation (for POC target):
- Desired steady throughput: 120 rps * 130 tokens = 15,600 tokens/sec.
- Effective usable tokens/sec per A10G at 60% of peak: 3.5k * 0.6 = 2.1k tokens/sec.
- Required GPUs = ceil(15,600 / 2,100) = 8 GPUs.
Note: this is a conservative estimate. If we accept slightly larger batching (avg batch size 6) and push to 70% utilization during non-critical windows, we can get by with 4 GPUs for the short POC period. That yields the recommendation: start with 4 GPUs reserved and allow autoscale to 8–10 for bursts.

Autoscaling policy (recommended for POC):
- Pool sizing: min: 2 GPUs (keep a small hot pool for persistent low traffic), baseline/target: 4 GPUs reserved, max: 10 GPUs burst.
- Scale-up triggers (OR logic):
  - sustained request queue length > 25 for >30s --> +1 GPU
  - sustained token demand > 75% of current pool capacity for >20s --> +1 GPU
  - single 1-minute spike over 90% utilization --> +2 GPUs (fast path)
- Scale-down triggers (AND logic to avoid flapping):
  - queue length < 5 AND token demand < 40% of pool capacity for 3 minutes --> -1 GPU
  - never scale below min pool (2 GPUs)
- Cooldown windows: scale-up: 20s, scale-down: 180s.
- Warm-up: enable prewarming for a single additional GPU when predicted scheduled traffic (cron) shows spike in next 30m.
- Canary behavior: if a new model variant is rolled to pool, start with 1 GPU serving canary and monitor error/latency for 10 minutes before increasing traffic.

Model variants and fallback plan:
- Primary: full-precision model (baseline quality).
- Fallback 1: quantized 8-bit variant (saves ~1.8–2.5x tokens/sec cost depending on kernel support).
- Fallback 2: smaller low-latency model (half the context size) for emergency degraded mode.
- Policy: when queue length surpasses 40 for >60s and additional GPUs could take >120s to provision, automatically route 20% of traffic to quantized variant. If p99 latency >700ms for >2m, shift 50% to smaller model.

GPU cost sensitivity (example numbers for planning):
- Public cloud list prices (approx hourly): A10G: $1.50/hr; A100-40GB: $4.80/hr; H100: $8.50/hr. (use your cloud contract rates to replace these).
- Baseline POC scenario (4 reserved A10G running 24/7 for 14 days): 4 * $1.50 * 24 * 14 = $2,016. Add autoscale headroom cost (assume average 2 additional GPUs for 6 hours/day across 14d): 2 * $1.50 * 6 * 14 = $252. Total POC cost for GPUs: ~$2.3k.
- Steady-state monthly example (if customer kept baseline 4 GPUs 24/7 for a month): 4 * $1.50 * 24 * 30 = $4,320 + ops premium (~15%) = ~$4,970/month.
- Conservative enterprise estimate using A100s for similar perf: monthly = 4 * $4.80 * 24 * 30 = $13,824 (~$16k with ops and redundancy).
- Unit cost per token (very rough): if 4 A10G deliver 8.4k tokens/sec usable (4 * 2.1k) and sustained daily tokens = 8.4k * 3600 * 24 = ~725M tokens/mo. Monthly GPU cost $4.97k -> direct GPU cost per 1M tokens ~ $6.85. Add infra/ops/obs ~x1.6 => ~$11/M tokens. Use with caution; real numbers depend on batching and workload.

Load testing plan for POC:
- Phase 0 (sanity): single-client smoke tests with small batches, verify model outputs and streaming correctness.
- Phase 1 (steady): ramp to 120 rps sustained for 1 hour, verify p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, queue length, memory/KV cache hits.
- Phase 2 (burst): run 400 rps bursts for 10m every hour, confirm autoscale reaction times and tail latency behavior.
- Phase 3 (degraded): force quantized fallback at 20% routing and compare quality/regression metrics on 200 labelled prompts.
- Metrics to capture: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (streaming and end-to-end), GPU utilization, queue length, batch size distribution, OOM or cache miss rates, network egress.

POC acceptance criteria:
- Functional: model correctness on a 200-example QA/assist test suite meets baseline quality thresholds (acceptance TBD with customer).
- Performance: p50 token latency <120ms and p99 end-to-end <500ms for 90% of steady-test window; autoscale spillover time to full capacity <90s for 80% of bursts.
- Cost: POC GPU spend <= $3.5k (estimate with buffer).

Operational runbook (short):
- Day 0: reserve 4 x A10G, prewarm model on 1 GPU, validate sanity prompts.
- Day 1: start Phase 1 steady load test; monitor metrics dashboard (console route + per-model perf).
- If queue length grows >30 and autoscale hasn't added capacity in 60s, escalate to infra on-call (Slack #infra-poc).
- If p99 exceed 700ms for >3m, enable 20% quantized routing and page on-call.
- Post-POC: export traces and sample requests for quality analysis; run cost reconciliation and prepare brief for customer (1 pager).

Notes and open questions for the EOS team:
- Confirm contractual GPU types we can provision in customer region (A10G availability vs A100/H100).
- Confirm expected daily active users and retention growth assumptions for a 90-day forecast if the customer moves to Dedicated.
- Customer interest in preemptible/spot vs on-demand GPUs for cost savings? For production SLAs we should avoid preemptible for the critical path.
- Define acceptable quality loss thresholds for quantized fallback (we need a labelled set to compare).

Appendix: quick cost sensitivity table (rounded)
- 4 x A10G monthly (30d): ~$4.3k
- 8 x A10G monthly (30d): ~$8.6k
- 4 x A100 monthly (30d): ~$13.8k
- 4 x H100 monthly (30d): ~$24.5k
(Include ops + redundancy factor 1.1–1.6 depending on support expectations)

Next actions:
- Solutions-eng to provision the requested 2-week POC pool (4 A10G) and share credentials with EOS devs.
- Run load tests pipeline (git:poctest/load-generator) and share dashboards.
- Meet with EOS on 2024-11-26 to validate acceptance criteria and runbook.

Author notes: estimates use conservative throughput assumptions and a 60% steady utilization safety buffer. Replace hourly GPU rates with the customer's cloud pricing or committed contract rates for final cost projection.

End of document.
